gaps.sentence: He's considering ___ his job and travelling for a year.
Instead of ___ , why don't you ask for help?
The children were excited ___ the circus.
gaps.explanation: 'Excited to see' — the to-infinitive follows the adjective.

gaps.sentence: We expect ___ the results by Friday.
gaps.explanation: expect takes the to-infinitive: expect to receive.

gaps.sentence: I can't wait ___ you the photos.
gaps.explanation: can't wait + to-infinitive: can't wait to show.

gaps.sentence: They can't help ___ at his impression of the boss.
gaps.explanation: can't help + -ing = can't stop yourself: can't help laughing.

gaps.sentence: She avoided ___ about the incident for weeks.
gaps.explanation: 'Avoid' is always followed by the -ing form.
